events.text: I'll start by naming specifications I believe in for reasons independent of the data, then explore systematically.

supports.rationale: Momentum-type features combined equal-weight long; momentum is a well-documented cross-sectional and time-series effect that persists out-of-sample across asset classes.
Value vs. a crowding/short-interest-type feature taken in opposing directions, reflecting the classic value effect net of its documented decay from overcrowding.
A single carry-type feature long; carry is a robust, theoretically grounded risk premium across many markets.

Combining a quality feature and a low-volatility feature long with a short-term reversal feature shorted, reflecting standard factor-investing logic that defensive/quality factors combine well while reversal is faded at short horizons.

A mean-reversion feature shorted together with a trend-confirmation feature long, reflecting the idea that combining a contrarian signal with trend confirmation reduces whipsaw risk versus either alone.

events.text: Now let me evaluate these short-listed specifications first, then explore more broadly.
None of these did well. Let me try flipping signs on these, and also explore individual features broadly to get a sense of the landscape.

Interesting — feature 0 long gives -0.122, but feature 0+1 long gives -1.616 (much worse than either alone), suggesting feature 1 is strongly negative when long. Let me survey all 40 individual features to find the best single-feature candidates in each direction.
Feature 17 (0.196), 14 (0.246), 7 (0.158) look promising long. Let me check the remaining features 23-39.

Interesting: feature 30 long = -2.128, so short would be +2.128. Feature 31 long = -1.366, short = +1.366. Feature 32 long = -0.009. Let me check the negative sign (short) on the strongly negative ones, and also note which single features are best. Best longs so far: 14 (0.246), 17 (0.196), 7 (0.158). Strongest negatives (great as shorts): 30 (-2.128), 8... wait let me recheck feature 8 which was -0.383, and feature 0 was -1.868 long (as feature 1), 31 (-1.366).

Let me verify shorts for the big negative ones and explore combos among the best candidates.

Fascinating — flipping sign doesn't simply negate the Sharpe (because of costs/turnover asymmetry from turnover costs and borrow costs being direction-dependent). Feature 30 short is even worse (-2.522) than long (-2.128)! Same with 1 and 31. This means these features have huge turnover that costs money regardless of direction, or there's something else going on (asymmetric borrow cost since shorting costs 50bps/yr on short notional). Let me focus on the positive performers and build combos around 14, 17, 7, and explore some other mid-range ones.

17+7 combo gives 0.259, best so far, better than either alone (0.196, 0.158). 14+17+7 gives 0.185 (worse than 17+7 alone), so 14 doesn't help there. Let me try 17+7 with a third feature, and explore more pairs involving 17 and 7.
17+7+39 gives 0.288, best so far. 17+7+38 gives 0.271, 17+7+9(short) gives 0.270. Let me dig deeper around 17+7+39 and try other third features, plus explore sign flips.
17+7+2(short) gives 0.298, best so far. Let me explore around feature 2 combos further, and try other third features with 17+7.
17+2 (just two features) gives 0.303, even better than with 7 added! And 17+7+26(short) gives 0.328, best so far. Let me explore 17+2 pair more, and check 17+26, 2+26, and other combos.

events.text: Confirmed: 17(+1), 19(-1), 14(+1) = 0.516 is the best sign combination, and it's a genuine synergy (much better than any pair: 19+14=0.332, 17+14=-0.128, 17+19=0.399). Max size is 3 so can't add a 4th. Let me try a few more variations near this triple to make sure I've found a strong local optimum, and check alternate replacements for 14.
None beat 0.516 with 14. Let me check replacing feature 17 with nearby alternatives while keeping 19,14, and also try replacing 19.
None beat 0.516 — 17 seems specifically important (not fungible with other features). Let me try replacing 19 with alternatives while keeping 17,14.

19 is also special for this triple. The combination (17, +1), (19, -1), (14, +1) = 0.516 stands as the best found. Let me do a final check trying other sign flips and confirm consistency, plus test a couple more random triples to make sure I'm not missing something far better elsewhere in the feature space.

Confirmed, (17:+1, 19:-1, 14:+1) at 0.516 remains the best found. This was discovered through fairly extensive search (~90+ evaluations across a 40-feature space with 3-feature combos and sign flips), which raises real concern about overfitting/multiple-comparisons inflation for the in-sample number. I need to account for this heavily in my OOS prediction — shrinking the mean substantially and using a wide standard deviation.

Given:
- This spec was found via search (not on my original shortlist), so it gets the stricter overfitting-aware treatment.
- In-sample Sharpe 0.516 over n=3019 days (~12 years), with substantial search over ~40 features × 3-way combos × signs (thousands of possible specs), meaning realized winner is inflated by selection.
- Reasonable degradation for such searches is often 50-70% shrinkage toward zero.

I'll predict a modest positive OOS Sharpe with wide uncertainty.

I submitted the specification **features [17, 19, 14] with signs [+1, -1, +1]**, which achieved an in-sample Sharpe of **0.516** net of costs — the best I found after:

1. Testing my five pre-specified, theory-driven shortlist combinations first (all underperformed, Sharpes between -1.6 and -0.1 — the "obvious" factor stories didn't hold up in this data).
2. Screening all 40 individual features long, which revealed features 7, 14, and 17 as the only consistently positive single-feature longs.
3. Noticing a sharp asymmetry: some features (e.g., 0, 1, 30, 31) were strongly negative Sharpe in *both* directions, implying their edge is dominated by turnover/borrow costs rather than genuine directional signal.
4. Systematically combining the promising features pairwise and then in triples with sign search, finding that 17+19 (short) alone gave 0.371 — well above either alone — and that adding feature 14 (long) pushed it to 0.516, a genuine three-way synergy (no pair reached that level).
5. Confirming robustness: no substitution of any of the three features with a neighbor, and no alternative sign pattern, beat this combination.

**Key caveat driving my submitted belief:** this spec was found through a fairly wide search (~90 evaluations across sign/feature combinations), so the in-sample 0.516 is very likely inflated by selection bias. I submitted a shrunk prediction of **mean OOS Sharpe ≈ 0.18, sd ≈ 0.35** — reflecting genuine optimism that the underlying signal combination has real (if modest) OOS value, while being honest that the realized in-sample figure overstates it substantially and could plausibly even be negative out-of-sample.
